added_lines: no later than thursday morning louisburgh church restoration and repair works since 2015 the south wall of the church and the bel l tower have suffered from significant water penetration (a problem first noted in the 1950s). internal render is breaking down, and paintwork is peeling off the walls. humidity levels in the building are high and water saturation of walls is reducing thermal performance making the building difficult to heat and maintain. investigative repo rts were carried out to identify and remedy the sources of moisture penetration. these included a measurement survey and structural , stained glass, services, asbestos, and building condition reports. temporary screens were erected to test the performance of the wall structure. a specialist conservation contractor carried out drill testing o f the walls which confirmed significant water-logging of wall cores. a conservation management plan was commissioned to guide the remedial works and to aid in making applications for grant funding. in february 2026 an application was made to mayo county council for permission to carry out repair works to remedy wall damp initially on 2 bays of the west wall, replace the bell tower roof and resurface the gravel path connecting the two entrances. in november 2026 an application will be made to mayo county council for grant funding to carry out these works under the historic structures fund and it is intended to begin restoration works in 2027. weekly collection envelopes: the weekly collection is used to pay the running expenses of the parish and the upkeep of parish property. an updated list is being prepared for 2027 if you do not currently use the envelope system and would like to contribute please return the attached form to the church. by using the envelopes we are able to avail of the revenue commissioners' income tax rebate scheme. parish of kilgeever i wish to receive a set of weekly envelopes to help contribute to the upkeep and running of my parish. name address our lady’s 15 promises to those who pray holy rosary the holy rosary is an enormous source of grace and spiritual protection, and one of the most powerful sacramentals of the catholic church. in particular, our lady has made fifteen specific promises to those wh o faithfully pray the rosary throughout their lives. we should yearn for these special graces—and you can r ead the exact promises below. but more than that, we should first remember that the rosary is a clear and easy path to sanctity. over the course of the rosary’s history, our lady h as appeared to saints and mystics to encourage devotio n to her and her son, especially through the rosary. 1. whoever shall faithfully serve me by the recitati on of the rosary, shall receive signal graces. 2. i promise my special protection and the greatest graces to all those who shall recite the rosary. 3. the rosary shall be a powerful armour against he ll, it will destroy vice, decrease sin, and defeat here sies. 4. it will cause virtue and good works to flourish; it will obtain for souls the abundant mercy of god; it will withdraw the hearts of men from the love of the world and its vanities, and will lift them to the desire of eternal things. oh, that souls would sanctify themselves by this means. 5. the soul which recommends itself to me by the recitation of the rosary shall not perish. 6. whoever shall recite the rosary devoutly, applying himself to the consideration of its sacred mysteries, shall never be conquered and never overwhelmed by misfortune. god will not chastise him in his justice, he shall not perish by an unprovided death; if he be j ust he shall grow in grace and become worthy of eternal life. 7. whoever shall have a true devotion for the rosary shall not die without the sacraments of the church. 8. those who are faithful to recite the rosary shal l have, during their life and at their death, the light of god and the plenitude of his graces; at the moment of death they shall participate in the merits of the saints in pa radise. 9. i shall deliver from purgatory those who have be en devoted to the rosary. 10. the faithful children of the rosary shall merit a high degree of glory in heaven. 11. you shall obtain all you ask of me by the recit ation of the rosary. 12. all those who propagate the holy rosary shall aided by me in their necessities. 13. i have obtained from my divine son that all the advocates of the rosary shall have for intercessors the entire celestial court during their life and at the hour of death. 14. all who recite the rosary are my sons and daughters, brothers and sisters of my only son jesus christ. 15. devotion of my rosary is a great sign of predestination. louisburgh (kilgeever)

2026 one in christ, united in mission this weekend, we celebrate mission sunday, a special day when catholics throughout the world come together in prayer & solidarity to support the church’s missionary work. this year marks the 100th anniversary of world mission sunday, established by pope pius xi in 1926. to mark this centenary, pope leo xiv has chosen the theme “one in christ, united in mission.” in his message for this special anniversary, pope leo reminds us that the mission of the church belongs to all of us. through baptism, every christian is called to share god's love & bring the message of the gospel to others. world mission sunday is an opportunity to remember the many missionaries who dedicate their lives to serving communities throughout the world, often in places facing great poverty & hardship. through our prayers, generosity & practical support, we can all play a part in their work. mission begins in our own everyday lives, through simple acts of kindness, compassion & care for others. together, we are one in christ & united in mission. athenry simanjiro partnership athenry–simanjiro partnership, first established in november 2005, is now in its 21st year. we are a registered charity. over the years, with the incredible generosity of the people of athenry & beyond, we've been able to support the community in simanjiro, north-east tanzania, in so many meaningful ways. celebrating our partnership: last year, fr. lawrence from simanjiro visited the parish. a wonderful display detailing the partnership's work is available to view in the church, a testament to athenry's generosity. making a real difference: the partnership directly connects with the local community to fund education & healthcare, with projects also including supplying fresh water & building the church. electricity only arrived there in 2021. a few things that make our partnership unique are: 100% direct donation: every single euro donated goes directly to simanjiro. self-funded travel: all who travel there pay their ownway – it's a core principle of the organisation. local partnership: we work proudly alongside our on-the- ground partners, the divine word missionaries, led by fr. bienvenue and fr. rex. support our future: thank you all once again for your kindness, generosity and commitment over the past 20 years. we look forward to continuing this wonderful partnership into the future. your support makes a real difference. if you would like to find out more, please see the board at the back of athenry church (which includes a donation box), is the holy father’s annual appeal for spiritual and financial support so that the life-giving work of overseas mission and missionaries can continue. it always falls on the second last sunday in october, meaning this year it will be celebrated over the weekend of sunday 18th october. world mission sunday collections take place in every single parish where the church is present. this includes not only ireland and europe, but also in poorer parishes in developing countries. it is a moment of universal solidarity when each member of the church family, regardless of location or background, play their part in supporting each other. this is what makes it such a special celebration. the theme for this year’s celebration of mission sunday is:“one in christ, united in mission.” the offertory collection at all masses this weekend will go to misso ireland , the irish branch of the pontifical missionary society. irish national synodal assembly - the working document for the irish national synodal assembly, taking place in gormanston, co meath, on 17 october, brings together the fruits of five years of prayer, listening and discernment and will guide delegates as they consider and vote on suggested actions to be presented to the bishops of ireland. while the assembly marks an important moment in the journey, the synodal pathway is now moving towards a new phase of implementation. everyone is invited to read, pray with, and reflect on the working document and the question: “what does god want from the church in ireland at this time?” please pray for all those taking part in the assembly and for the guidance of the holy spirit, and scan the qr code to access the working document and find out more, and see
